series: Eurasia Group Top Risks: year-end self-assessments
about: Eurasia Group's own year-end reviews of its Top Risks. These are the publisher's claims about its own record, quoted in its words. Hindsight has not graded them. No score or letter grade is published; verdicts are prose.

found.2018: Video only: 'Top Risks 2018: how did we do?' (https://www.eurasiagroup.net/live-post/top-risks-2018-how-did-we-do). No text transcript; not captured.

not_found: No year-end review found for editions 2007-2017, 2019-2021 or 2023. Searched: eurasiagroup.net live-posts and the Wayback Machine URL index for eurasiagroup.net and gzeromedia.com. A 'revisiting the top geopolitical risks of 2025' video (https://www.gzeromedia.com/video/ask-ian/revisiting-the-top-geopolitical-risks-of-2025) has no transcript on the page. Web search was unavailable during capture, so reviews published elsewhere may exist.

entries.verdict: Bremmer, Kupchan, and EG’s China team were warning that China’s lockdown and testing intensive zero-COVID policy would last longer than many expected, would inflict considerable pain on China’s economy, and would stoke social unrest.
entries.verdict_section: So, what did Eurasia Group get right?
entries.reviewer: GZERO Media (Eurasia Group's media company), analysis by a Eurasia Group director

entries.verdict: They also saw that China’s problems in 2022 would extend well beyond COVID, even as leader Xi Jinping consolidated more power.
entries.verdict_section: So, what did Eurasia Group get right?
entries.reviewer: GZERO Media (Eurasia Group's media company), analysis by a Eurasia Group director

entries.verdict: They were right that Brazil’s election might generate controversy and even violence, but that a peaceful transfer of power would follow.

entries.verdict: Finally, though there was no new flow of refugees from the Middle East into Europe, missing the full-on Russian invasion meant missing the flow of millions of Ukrainians into Poland and other neighboring countries.
